citation: "The Old Kinzie Mansion in 1832." — wood engraving, the upper panel of a plate with "Chicago in 1845, from the West", in George F. Cram, Cram's Standard American Railway System Atlas of the World / Columbian World's Fair Atlas (Chicago: George F. Cram, 1893).
author: Blomgren Bros. & Co., engravers, for George F. Cram's atlas; the artist is not named on the plate
repository: David Rumsey Map Collection, via Internet Archive; the copy held in this repository is chicago/reference/images/chicago/chicago_kinzie_mansion_1832_and_1845_view.jpg (catalogued in chicago/reference/images/IMAGE_SOURCES.md)
locator: the upper panel, about x 290-980, y 112-550 px of the 1280 x 881 px page held here; captioned under it
rights_note: Published 1893 in the United States, out of copyright by age; the Rumsey scan is offered as public domain.
access_notes: Read off the image file itself on 2026-10-15 (T-2498). The atlas page number was not reached from the run's container, so none is cited.
what_it_supplies: the house long and low under a gable roof along the river, its west gable toward the eye
two stacks through the ridge, about 0.44 and 0.92 of it from the west gable
a piazza across the whole front, its roof drawn as the main roof carried down in one plane
a central door with two sash either side under the piazza
a picket fence round the green before the house, four columnar poplars in a row east of it, and a great tree behind
a two-storey house and a shed behind it to the north-west, in 1832
what_it_does_not_supply: the house in 1812: it dates itself to 1832
note: Close in composition to the 1857 Chicago Magazine engraving and probably redrawn from the same tradition; it agrees with that engraving on the stacks and the poplars and with Lossing on the one-plane piazza roof. Its camera and match record are data/reference_views/kinzie_house_1812/cram_1893.json.
